clue.text: Found out about clues construction — no Latin and lacking definition

indicators.note: about places the first set of letters round the second
out signals that the letters of the word found are put in disarray
construction says the remaining letters are built up afresh in a new order
no says a letter is dropped from the word clues

explanation.surface: A crossword critic complains that the clues are vague, lacking Latin and any clear definition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' and 'no' Latin rework the clue word minus its L; 'about' wraps the rearranged FOUND (UNFOD) round that, after UNFO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfocused is blurred, lacking sharp definition, as a photograph might be.

clue.text: Excited hearts, in faith, plenty of which at NASA launch

definitions.text: plenty of which at NASA launch

parts.note: to be up is to be excited or stirred

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: faith and trust are synonyms
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: At a NASA launch, hearts race with excitement and faith in the mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: a rocket launch needs a great deal of upward force.
explanation.definitionFit: Upthrust is upward force, which a rocket needs in abundance at lift-off.

clue.text: Leisure money once raised, losing large resources

parts.note: leisure is time for fun

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
losing says one letter is removed

parts.note: LSD (pounds, shillings and pence) was Britain's pre-decimal money
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An old pot of leisure money was raised but lost a large sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's money before 1971 was pounds, shillings and pence (librae, solidi, denarii); 'losing' drops the L before 'raised' turns the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds are money resources available for spending.

clue.text: Switch cricketer playing with bra without underwired insert tops

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with
tops picks the first letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A cricketer is fooling around with a bra lacking its underwired insert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' gives U and I from 'underwired insert', and 'playing' shuffles them with CRICKETER and BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit breaker is an automatic electrical switch that cuts the current.

clue.text: New dates accepted by car producer, Fish

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside another piece

parts.note: Saab is a Swedish carmaker
D is an abbreviation for date, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: New dates have been agreed by a car manufacturer called Fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dab is a small flatfish of the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Sporting no tie when entertained by colonial administrator is duty related

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside another piece

parts.note: DC stands for District Commissioner, a colonial administrator

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters are frolicking into a new order

explanation.surface: Being tieless when hosted by a colonial official was a matter of etiquette and duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' rearranges NO TIE as EONTI, which sits between D and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Deontic is a philosophical term for things concerning obligation or duty.

clue.text: See 25
Rider means group of plotters has new role

parts.note: a cabal is a secret group of plotters

indicators.note: new says the letters of role are made anew

explanation.surface: A rider explains that a band of conspirators has given him a fresh part to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish horseman, a rider.

clue.text: Roll on stages between two points

indicators.note: between places the second piece in the middle of the first

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point; two of them give EE
laps are stages of a race

explanation.surface: A race rolls on through its stages between two checkpoints.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll on, said of time, is to pass by or slip away.

clue.text: "Echo-cerebral" ET activity, which enables connection with earth

indicators.note: activity suggests the letters are busily moving about

explanation.surface: An alien's echoing brainwaves let it make contact with Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activity' shuffles the letters of ECHO-CEREBRAL and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-core cable has live, neutral and an earth wire, allowing an earth connection.

clue.text: Somebody into transitive cosmetic preparation

indicators.note: into means put inside the following piece

parts.note: TR is the dictionary abbreviation for transitive
one can mean a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Someone is getting into a cosmetic preparation, as if transitively.
explanation.definitionFit: A toner is a cosmetic lotion applied to tighten the skin.

clue.text: Its sufferer would have nothing new

definitions.text: Its sufferer would have nothing new

parts.words: Its sufferer would have nothing new
parts.note: read literally, a person with a dread of novelty would refuse anything new

explanation.definitionFit: Neophobia is the fear of new things, so a sufferer shuns novelty.

clue.text: How a note is heard to ring

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
something heard is a sound

explanation.surface: A question of how a musical note rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is a link word: RE's sound is how that note is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound is to ring or echo loudly.

clue.text: Oddly torn by sex psychologist Rose's support?

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: Havelock Ellis was a pioneering British sex psychologist

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose, torn apart, turns to a sex psychologist for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; it is the climbing flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice frame supporting climbing plants such as roses.

clue.text: Ordinary model's lowly successor gets protected status (sexually ambivalent turn)

parts.note: safety is the state of being protected
bi is short for bisexual
a cycle is a turn or revolution

explanation.surface: A model gets protection while undergoing a sexually ambivalent change.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ordinary' was the penny-farthing; the lower-slung safety bicycle replaced it.
explanation.definitionFit: The safety bicycle, with its low frame, succeeded the high-wheeled 'ordinary' or penny-farthing.

clue.text: Gold-digger's enemies drug-free — not so good

indicators.note: free here means without, so a letter goes

parts.note: foes are enemies
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
sicker means more ill, not so good

explanation.surface: A gold-digger's enemies have given up drugs, but feel worse for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold-digger' suggests a fortune hunter; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossicker searches for gold, especially in Australian old workings.

clue.text: It makes tracks available to us, courtesy of foreign sportsman with protected status?

definitions.text: It makes tracks available to us

parts.note: CD (corps diplomatique) marks diplomats, who enjoy protected status
a player is a sportsman

explanation.surface: A foreign sportsman with diplomatic protection lays down tracks for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' hints at the diplomats behind CD; 'courtesy of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A CD player plays the tracks on a compact disc.

clue.text: Bricklaying method to carry an injured agent?

parts.note: a stretcher is used to carry an injured person
James Bond is the fictional secret agent

explanation.surface: A question of how to carry an injured secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretcher bond is a brick pattern with all bricks laid lengthwise, overlapping by half.

clue.text: Trunk touches hand's third digit without one twisting

indicators.note: without means outside, so the pieces surround a letter

parts.note: the torso is the trunk of the body
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: third digit points to the third letter of the word

explanation.surface: A body touches a hand's ring finger while missing one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' suggests a finger; here it is the third character of 'hand', N, which joins TORSO before I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, as of a metal bar.

clue.text: Element adding aura to army officer

parts.note: a halo is a glowing aura
Gen is short for general, an army officer

explanation.surface: An army officer gains a saintly aura.
explanation.definitionFit: The halogens are a group of chemical elements, so a halogen is an element.

clue.text: Electronic tester for collapsible ladder

parts.note: one who tries something out is testing it

explanation.surface: An electronic gadget is used to test a folding ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: An étrier is a short rope ladder used in climbing, which folds up.

clue.text: Prelude to alopecia is losing height: it's not good for inspiration

indicators.note: is losing means a letter drops out

parts.note: thin hair comes before baldness (alopecia)

explanation.surface: Losing height before going bald is no help to inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' is breathing in: air at altitude is poor for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin air, at high altitude, has little oxygen, so is poor for breathing in.

clue.text: Ostracise, after losing two books, an archaic, destitute person

indicators.note: after losing means letters are dropped

parts.note: to blackball is to exclude or ostracise
B is the abbreviation for book, so two books are BB

explanation.surface: An archaic pauper is ostracised after losing two books.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack-all is an old word for someone who has nothing, a destitute person.

clue.text: One day, William raised less money, so extemporised

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: less means a letter is subtracted
raised in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Bill is short for William
L stands for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: One day William raised less money than planned, so he improvised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BILL to LLIB; 'less' L leaves LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak without preparation, to extemporise.

clue.text: Licensee's work lacks new fitting

indicators.note: lacks means a letter is missing

parts.note: a publican, holding a licence, runs an inn

explanation.surface: A publican's work has little new that is appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in keeping is appropriate or consistent, fitting.

clue.text: Beef pot by top grade cook Forte rejected

parts.note: a pot belly is a belly, pot meaning paunch
A is the top grade

indicators.note: rejected means a letter is thrown out

parts.note: a chef is a cook
F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: A beef pot with top-grade quality is turned down by cook Forte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forte' looks like the hotelier's name; it is the musical term, F.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is to complain, as is to bellyache.

clue.text: Terror tactics housing fraud

indicators.note: housing means these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Terror tactics conceal a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Rort is Australian slang for a fraudulent scheme or scam.

clue.text: UK's EEC role as a result of De Gaulle's position: on a limb

parts.note: De Gaulle vetoed Britain's entry, French non
a member is a limb

explanation.surface: Britain was left out on a limb of the EEC because De Gaulle said no.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles de Gaulle vetoed British entry to the EEC in 1963 and 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-member is outside an organisation, as Britain was outside the EEC.
